sets.g: Passage A represents a formal and considered message from the Governors letting the applicant know that they were successful. The language is formal and precise. The response to this message must equally be formal and kindly, though perhaps distant and deferential. Passage B represents a less formal message to the applicant. Equally positive, it is more familiar and casual. It is likely that the sender and the applicant know each other at least a little bit. As such, the response is perhaps slightly bold, familiar in return.
sets.p:
A. Thank you for your application. We are delighted to inform you that the panel of Governors have accepted your paper for presentation at the conference. Please respond to this message, confirming your intention to display the paper at the event.
B. I thoroughly enjoyed reading your paper. It was very thoughtful, and it should not come as a great surprise that I pushed for its acceptance for the conference. I look forward to catching up with you, give me a call when you arrive.
i: I gratefully accept your offer to present my paper at the conference. Thank you for this opportunity.
A
This response is on point, formal, deferential and gracious = A
Thanks for helping me out with this one. I will see you there, I will be wearing my white tuxedo.
B

This response infers that the sender and applicant known each other. They have an equal status, and the language is not formal. Particular attention can be paid to the phrase ‘wearing my white tuxedo.’ Rather than just a tuxedo, the use of ‘my’ is deliberate to indicate that the person receiving this response is aware or has seen this white tuxedo beforehand. This is more evidence of the familiar relationship between the two correspondents = B
This is great to hear! Thanks for this – I owe you one.
B
Very causal and very familiar. “Thanks,” is a casual expression of gratitude, and saying “I owe you one,” clearly infers that the sender and applicant know each other well = B
It is with great pleasure that I hear this welcome news. You have my sincerest gratitude for accepting my paper.
A
The language is fluffy with undue graciousness and reverence. Very formal and reserved = A
Lovely to hear back from you. I will, of course, accept your offer and am delighted to present my paper for the conference.
B

The language is polite and formal, it is also quite distant. Although it is friendly, and the phrase “lovely to hear back from you,” implies, at least slightly, that they are on good terms, it fits better with the casualness of passage B rather than the formal tone of A = B

sets.p: The Governors’ Ball was a great success. The paper presentations were engaging and thoughtful. However, there was (few / no / some / several) confusion with what was considered (appropriate / necessary / well-fitted) attire. While some of the guests wore formal dress, others (war / were / wore) sports gear. This has caused some concern regarding the wording of our invitation (as / if / therefore / this) clearly there has been some miscommunication.
i: “However, there was (few / no / several / some) confusion…”
Few
No
Several
Some
D

While answer B works, it negates the rest of the passage, as there clearly was some confusion. ‘Confusion’ is an abstract noun. Therefore, answers A and C provide too specific amount of quantifiable ‘confusion’. We need to use a quantifier that works with abstract nouns. The only possibility is D. “There was some confusion”.
“What was considered (appropriate / necessary / well-fitted) attire.”
Appropriate
Necessary
Well-fitted
A

The attire people were to wear had some confusion. Given that context, there needed to be attire that was okay to wear in the situation. In other words, appropriate. Necessary attire does not make much sense. Well-fitted attire, while possible, seems odd in context of the rest of the passage. People were wearing different styles of clothing. The problem was not that they were well-fitted, it was whether they were appropriate.
“While some of the guests wore formal dress, others (war / were / wore) sports gear.”
War
Were
Wore
C

This question revolves around the spelling of different types of ‘war’ words in English. Each word means something different of course. The correct spelling is ‘wore’ which is the past continuous of ‘to wear’.
“This has caused some concern regarding the wording of our invitation (as / if / therefore / this) clearly there has been some miscommunication”.
As
If
Therefore
This
A

Given the context, the word is used mid-sentence which gives emphasis to the word ‘clearly’. ‘If clearly’ is inelegant and confusing in the sentence. ‘Therefore’ and ‘this’ do not make much grammatical sense either mid-sentence. ‘As’ puts the emphasis on the other words and is grammatically correct.

sets.p: The school has a long history of steamed alumni that covers over two centuries. The Governors’ Board has often remained behind the scenes, steering the school thorough turbulent times and provided the necessary funds for projects. I have admirable many on the board for their diligence over the years, and it is with great pleasure that I announce that next school term, I shall be joining this distinguished companies. I will endeavour to uphold the values of the school as well as the high standard with which the Governors hold.
i: “The school has a long history of steamed alumni that covers over two centuries.”
Esteemed
‘Steamed’ is the past of ‘to steam’ which is a peculiar action regarding alumni. The word needed is ‘esteemed’ which refers to someone or something held in high regard.
“Steering the school thorough turbulent times”
Through

This is a deceptive spelling error that changes the word from ‘through’ to ‘thorough’, completely changing the meaning. ‘Through turbulent times’ is the correct phrase which makes grammatical sense rather than ‘thorough turbulent times’.
“I have admirable many on the board”
Admired
‘Admirable’ leaves the sentence grammatically incorrect. It needs to be changed to the present perfect simple = I have ‘admired’.
“I shall be joining this distinguished companies.”
Company
The plural is used at the end of sentence, leaving the intended meaning and little eschewed. The correct answer is the singular = company.

sets.p:
Presented are a variety of responses you have received from the board of Governors regarding the proposals you have put forward to them.

A. Firstly, I would like to welcome you to the board. Secondly, I would like to state for the record that I think this idea has no merit and would actively oppose it at the earliest opportunity.
B. I like this idea, I think there is something to it. Let me get back to you after I contemplate it further.
C. Great idea, though unfortunately you might not be aware of our current budget situation – there is no way this can be implemented in time.
D. I do not see how this will add any value to us, or the board. I am very hesitant about your proposal.
E. I am very impressed – this is the kind of thinking this board drastically needs. I will completely support you with this idea.
i: Firstly, I would like to welcome you to the board. Secondly, I would like to state for the record that I think this idea has no merit and would actively oppose it at the earliest opportunity.
5th
This is the most negative of the statements. The Governor is actively opposed to the idea proposed. No other statement is completely against the idea. Therefore, it ranks as E.
I like this idea, I think there is something to it. Let me get back to you after I contemplate it further.
2nd
This is one of the more positive responses. The Governor likes the idea and thinks it can work – unlike most of the other responses. However, it is not the most positive, and, thus is B.
Great idea, though unfortunately you might not be aware of our current budget situation – there is no way this can be implemented in time.
3rd
This response is ambivalent. It is slightly positive, yet is negative against the idea from happening. This fits in the middle of our ranking, and, thus is C.
I do not see how this will add any value to us, or the board. I am very hesitant about your proposal.
4th
This response is negative and does not like the idea. However, it is not going to resist the idea like in response 1. The is the second most negative, and as such, is D.
I am very impressed – this is the kind of thinking this board drastically needs. I will completely support you with this idea.
1st
This is clearly the most positive of the responses – being the only way that will back it completely. Therefore, this is the tops the ranking with A.

sets.p: The Governors’ Ball will start at 19:00. Most attendees have already purchased a ticket online for collection at the door. However, one can buy a ticket on the door for a premium price of £12.50. Each attendee will be given one free cocktail from a choice of Daiquiri, Martini, or Margarita. After which, attendees may purchase drinks from the upstairs gallery. The speeches are due to commence at 20:00.
i: Every attendant is given one free cocktail from the upstairs gallery.
Cannot Say
Cannot Say - Though the passage states that every attendant will receive one free cocktail, it does not specify where. As such, we cannot know for definitely and cannot say.
Most attendees will buy tickets at the door for £12.50
False
False - The second line in the passage “most attendees have already purchased a ticket online” which contradicts the question statement. Therefore, it is false.
All attendees will have the option to receive one free Manhattan cocktail.
False
False - The fourth line of the passage “a choice of Daiquiri, Martini, or Margarita” which excludes a Manhattan cocktail. Therefore, the question statement is false.
After the speeches commence, they are due to run for two hours.
Cannot Say
Cannot Say - There is no mention of the speech duration in the passage. Therefore, we cannot say.
The upstairs gallery will provide drinks for the attendees.
True
True - The fifth line of the passage states that attendees may purchase drinks for the upstairs gallery. Therefore, the question statement is true.

sets.g: Passage A represents a formal and considered message, letting the applicant know that they were successful and offering them a position. The language is formal and professional. The response to this message must equally be formal and kindly, though perhaps distant and deferential. Passage B represents a less formal message to the applicant. Equally positive, it is more familiar and casual. It is likely that the sender and the applicant know each other at least a little bit. As such, the response is perhaps slightly bold, familiar in return.
sets.p:
A. Your findings were assessed anonymously by the panel in order to best remove bias and groupthink. In conclusion, we were thoroughly impressed by your work and would love to offer you a position here effective immediately. Please reply within a week to discuss further details with regards to this opportunity.
B. The panel looked over your report and, if I am honest with you, the results were very encouraging. We really liked section B, which I found particularly interesting, and parts of section C. It pleases me to say that we would like you to join us as soon as possible. Let me know when’s best, thanks.
i: Thank you very much for getting back to me so promptly. It is with great joy that I would like to accept your offer for the position and will endeavour to bring the highest of standards where I may.
A
This response is fluffy in language, formal, deferential and gracious and thus a more appropriate response to passage A.
Great to hear from you! That all sounds fantastic. I am free to come in tomorrow morning if that works for you?
B
This response infers that the sender and applicant know each other well. They have an equal status, and the language is very casual = B.
Thank you for your kind offer. Unfortunately, I must decline your generous offer due to unforeseen circumstances. My sincerest apologies.
A

The language is very professional. It is distant and emotionally reserved. The phrase is also filled with precise words that seem carefully constructed rather than throwaway. This response suits passage A.
Thank you for your offer. It perhaps comes as no surprise that I would love to accept. It sounds fun and it would be good to work on something together.
B
The language is friendly. Though it appears quite formal, it seems like the applicant is familiar or on good terms with the employer. As such, it better relates to passage B as a response.
Thanks for getting back to me so quickly – I would be honoured to join you and your panellists as soon as possible.
B
The language is formal and distant, but it is perfunctory and not particularly well-suited as a professional response. As such, it better represents passage B.

sets.p: The business is (ran / run / wrung) by a dozen individuals who make up ‘the panel’. Currently, they are looking (for / through / with) new research projects to undertake that will help them gain (further / longer / wider) insight into their trade and bestows / issues / provides / new approaches to (expand / propel / stretch) their business.
i: “The business is (run / ran / wrung) by a dozen individuals…”
Ran
Run
Wrung
B

‘Ran’ is the past tense of the verb ‘to run’. This does not grammatically work in the passage that is in the present. ‘Wrung’ is a red-herring that does not make sense in the sentence. The correct word is ‘run’, the present tense, ‘the business is run by a dozen individuals…’
“They are looking (for / through / with) new research projects…”
For
Through
With
A

To look ‘with’ needs an object to look with. Research projects do not make sense in that erroneous context. Likewise with ‘through’. In the context of the passage, the business is looking ‘for’ new research projects – which works correctly.
“Will help them gain (further / wider / longer) insight…”
Further
Longer
Wider
A

To gain wider insight is an incorrect expression, as is longer insight, which does not particularly make sense. To gain further insight is to understand something at a deeper level. Therefore, further is the correct choice.
“(Provides / issues / bestows) new approaches…”
Bestows
Issues
Provides
C

‘Bestows’ indicates that the new approaches were somehow given from a higher power. While perhaps possible, it seems odd in this context. ‘Issues’ indicates a similar sentiment though perhaps subtly more legislative. ‘Provides’ suggests to give, whether consequentially or not, these new approaches in the preferred manner.
“To (expand / propel / stretch) their business.”
Expand
Propel
Stretch
A

To ‘propel’ a business does not make sense. To ‘stretch’ a business, while possible, does not describe this situation. In this context, the business or growing, rather ‘expanding’. Therefore, ‘expand’ is the correct word to use.

sets.p: As you may well be aware, I have a long carrier in business. Having started a few notable tech start-ups, I now act as business consultant for sum companies in the financial district. I wish to send you my thanks for accepting me as you’re newest member. I know that a few of you has your initial reversions, but rest issued, I will give my utmost to not let you down.
i: “I have a long carrier in business.”
Career
‘Carrier’ makes this sentence somewhat nonsensical. The word that is desired is ‘career’, which requires a spelling change to determine.
“Act as business consultant for sum companies”
Some
‘Sum’ companies needs to be replaced by ‘some’. The spelling error changes the meaning of the sentence in a way that creates confusion.
“Thanks for accepting me as you’re newest member”
Your
The classic you’re/your grammar obstacle. You are newest member does not make sense. The context requires possession. As such, the correct answer needed is ‘your’.
“A few of you has your initial”
Had
This is a tense change from ‘has’ to ‘had’ to refer to something that has happened.
“Initial reversions,”
Reservations
This correction is a spelling change from an incorrect word, ‘reversions’ to ‘reservations’. It is a subtle but necessary change.
“But rest issued, I will give my utmost to not let you down.”
Assured
‘But rest issued’ does not make much sense. The common expression is ‘rest assured’, to provide some comfort to a situation. Therefore, we need to change ‘issued’ to ‘assured’.

sets.p:
You have prepared the following responses to an invitation to a meeting, which you are unable to attend due to previous commitments.

A. Unfortunately, I am not able to make the meeting due to being out of the country. I will be returning in four days, and we can catch-up then. Thanks.
B. A meeting on such short notice is a terrible suggestion. I do not think that is a good idea and will not be attending.
C. Okay, I will see you tomorrow morning for the meeting. However, I will be a little late due to planned delays on public transport.
D. A meeting tomorrow morning sounds good for me. I look forward to finally meeting you.
E. Great idea – you do not have to worry about me, I shall be there early.
i: Unfortunately, I am not able to make the meeting due to being out of the country. I will be returning in four days, and we can catch-up then. Thanks.
4th

This response aims to be very neutral. It does not give much of an opinion on the meeting, but simply informs the latest member that they will not be attending. The other responses are more positive than this one though so it must rank 4th.
A meeting on such short notice is a terrible suggestion. I do not think that is a good idea and will not be attending.
5th

This response is extremely negative about the meeting and the idea. The word ‘terrible’ helps express the negativity of feeling from this response. Therefore, this is ranked the most negative, which is 5th.
Okay, I will see you tomorrow morning for the meeting. However, I will be a little late due to planned delays on public transport.
3rd

This response is neutral, though it aims to give off a good impression. It is factual and formal – not negative and dismissive. This neutrality places it squarely in the centre of the ranking, which is 3rd.
A meeting tomorrow morning sounds good for me. I look forward to finally meeting you.
2nd
This is a positive response and is friendly in tone. However, it is not the most emphatically positive, therefore it ranks below the top, which is 2nd.
Great idea – you do not have to worry about me, I shall be there early.
1st
This is clearly the most positive of the responses – very friendly and casual, expressing enthusiasm towards the idea of the meeting. Therefore, this tops the ranking at the 1st position.

sets.p: The meeting will commence at 07:30 on the second floor of the Shaftsbury building. Coffee, tea and croissants will be available before and during the meeting. Each panel member must follow the seating plan, where their name will be identifiable at the chair’s head. The meeting will last for two hours and will cover most imminent business matters, as well as the introduction of our newest member.
i: The panel members will be given paninis before the meeting.
False
False – The passage states that before the meeting “coffee, tea and croissants will be available...”, not paninis. Therefore, this is false.
There are not enough chairs for each panel member.
False
False - The passage that each panel member will have an assigned chair. Therefore, there is the precise number of chairs. Therefore, it is false.
The meeting will take place on the second floor.
True
True - In the first line of the passage is states that the meeting will take place on the “second floor of the Shaftsbury building”. Therefore, this is true.
The meeting will start by introducing the newest member of the panel.
Cannot Say
Cannot Say - There is no mention how the meeting is going to start. Therefore, we cannot say.
The meeting will last for more than one and a half hours.
True
True - The fourth line of the passage states that the meeting will last for two hours, which is longer than one and a half hours. Therefore, the question statement is true.

sets.g: Passage A represents a formal and considered message. The language is serious and professional. The response to this message must equally be formal and kindly, though perhaps distant and deferential. Passage B represents a less formal message to the applicant. Though serious, it is more familiar and less strict in its use of language. It is likely that the sender and the applicant know each other at least a little bit. As such, the response is perhaps slightly bold, familiar in return.
sets.p:
A. Due to the sensitive nature of our work, absolute discretion is vital. We greatly appreciate your interest in this position and will get back to you once we have had time to look over your application. You should not discuss this with anyone other than a close family member.
B. As you may know, although it is great you sent us an application for the upcoming position, I must ask that you do not tell anyone about this if that is alright? It is just that it is important that no one knows. It is not information the public should have access to.
i: Got it. I will make sure that nobody finds out about all of this.
B
This response is direct but informal. The phrase ‘got it’ is not a particularly professional response. This is better suited for passage B.
I will of course endeavour with the upmost caution to maintain the security of the information.
A
The language is eloquent and extravagant, and maintains an element of professionalism. Therefore, this is better suited as a response for passage A.
Alright, I get where you are coming from. You have nothing to worry about, I have got you covered.
B
The language is very casual, friendly and familiar. Perhaps they know each other. Much better for passage B.
Naturally, it goes without saying that you keep your information private. I promise not to tell anyone.
B
The phrase ‘it goes without saying’ is quite informal. Therefore, this is more appropriate as a response to passage B.
No one shall know about my application. The security regarding this matter is of the upmost importance to me.
A
The language is formal and reserved. ‘Upmost importance’ emphasises a sense of professional and urgency. It is not casual. This response is better suited to passage A.

sets.p: Intelligence operations are at the (brain / hand / heart) of what we do. Fundamental to (their / these / there) operations are people. It is important to understand how people work and (how / what / why) you can do to motivate or handle them. As such, (extrapersonal / interpersonal / intrapersonal) skills are absolutely necessary. Other requirements include: curiosity and complex problem solving.
i: “Intelligence operations are at the (brain / hand / heart) of what we do.”
Brain
Hand
Heart
C
The options describe different bodily organs. The expression is with ‘heart’ which means that core or the main idea. Therefore, it should be ‘are at the heart of what we do’.
“Fundamental to (their / there / these) operations are people.”
Their
There
These
C

‘There’ does not make much sense, so that can be discounted. ‘Their’ operations, while possible, places a strange emphasis on the possessiveness of the operations. Compared to ‘these’ operations, which places the focus on the category of operations, it seems less fluent as ‘these’.
“How people work and (how / what / why) you can do…”
How
What
Why
B
‘Why’ and ‘how’ do not make much sense in the context of the sentence. The only possible workable answer is ‘what’, leading to ‘what you can do’ – the correct answer.
“As such, (extrapersonal / interpersonal / intrapersonal) skills are absolutely necessary.”
Extrapersonal
Interpersonal
Intrapersonal
B

‘Interpersonal’ is to communicate with other people. ‘Intrapersonal’ is something in the mind, and ‘extrapersonal’ is a colloquial word, outside the person – not applicable. In the context of the sentence, ‘interpersonal skills’, as in the ability to talk well with others, is the correct answer.

sets.p: About a week ago, I applyed for a position in security. I request your kind assistance helping me with references. Since then, I had heard of several great letters from some of you. In the interim, I thought I would send a kind reminder to those of you who have forgotten. I am most thankful for your vote for confidence.
i: “I applyed for a position in security.”
Applied
There is a spelling error with ‘applyed’ which should be ‘applied’.
“Since then, I had heard of several great letters”
Have
Given the context of the sentence, following ‘since then,’ the tense needs changing from ‘had’ to ‘have’.
“I thought I would send a kind reminder to those of you who have forgotten”
Whom
Subtle error – who is to identify the subject. In this case, we need ‘whom’ which is used to refer to an object; the ones who have forgotten.
“I am most thankful for your vote for confidence.”
Of
Your ‘vote for confidence’ does not make much sense. The correct expression is ‘vote of confidence.’ Therefore, we need to change ‘for’ to ‘of’.

sets.p:
A. Thank you for taking time out of your day to come have this interview. However, you are not what we are looking for this time around.
B. Unfortunately, you are not good enough to do this role and I would advise you against applying for next year’s intake.
C. Thank you for your presence at the interview. I think though that you would be better suited to almost anything else.
D. It gives me joy to announce that you are exactly the kind of candidate that we are looking for.
E. Thank you, you are a strong candidate and we would like to offer you the position.
i: Thank you for taking time out of your day to come have this interview. However, you are not what we are looking for this time around.
3rd
The language is friendly in tone though negative in its message. As such, it is ambivalent. Given the other passages, this sits in the middle. = C
Unfortunately, you are not good enough to do this role and I would advise you against applying for next year’s intake.
5th
The phrase ‘you are not good enough’ is particularly indelicate. As such, this is the most negative of the phrases. = E
Thank you for your presence at the interview. I think though that you would be better suited to almost anything else
4th
This response is very negative, almost sarcastic in its delivery. It narrowly misses out on the most negative, simply because the other phrase is a little more personally unfriendly. = D
It gives me joy to announce that you are exactly the kind of candidate that we are looking for.
1st
This is a positive response and is friendly in tone. The word ‘joy’ expresses great enthusiasm. As such, this is most positive response. = A
Thank you, you are a strong candidate and we would like to offer you the position
2nd
This is a positive response. It is not quite as joyous as response 4, and as such is just below in the ranking = B

sets.p: The operation will take place in three days’ time at 04:50, at Howard Hotel. Our first port of call is to have personnel on the ground floor gathering intel by 05:00. After 15 minutes, Team A will have moved to the first floor whilst Team B will remain on the ground floor. The package swap will take place in the basement of the kitchen. The target will be located in the penthouse.
i: By 05:15. Team A will be at the first floor.
True
True – Line 2 says that Team A will be at the ground floor at 05:00. Line 3 says that they will be at the first floor 15 minutes later = 05:15.
The target refers to an individual.
Cannot Say
Cannot Say – There is no reference to whether the target refers to an individual. Therefore, we cannot say.
Team B will have occupied the first floor by 05:00.
False
False – Line 3 states that Team B will remain on the ground floor. Therefore, the statement is false.
The penthouse of George Hotel is where the target will be located.
False
False – The passage says that the operation will be at the Howard Hotel, not the George Hotel.
By 05:30, the target will be in the basement of the kitchen.
Cannot Say
Cannot Say – While the passage says that the package will be in the basement, it says nothing about the location of the target. Therefore, we cannot say.
